summary: Records a short segment of CHOP input while a listen signal is on, then trims, blends, and loops the captured gesture in time.
key_concepts: Records the first input while the listen input is above zero, passes input through during recording, then loops the captured segment once listening stops.
The second input is the listen gate and the third input is the reset trigger, so wiring order is part of the operator contract.
Fit to Nearest Cycle extends or trims the captured gesture to a multiple of Beats per Cycle; with it off, the loop length is the recorded duration.
Blend Time creates a loop crossfade between the segment end and start, while Interpolate Samples controls resampling during speed or duration changes.
Sequential Play Mode exposes reset behavior through Reset Condition, Reset, and Reset Pulse, while Locked to Timeline follows timeline position.

key_params.name: playmode
key_params.note: Locked to timeline or sequential playback

key_params.name: fitmethod
key_params.note: Fit captured gesture to nearest beat cycle

key_params.name: step
key_params.note: Step output each cycle to avoid jumps

key_params.name: resetcondition
key_params.note: How third input resets the gesture

common_gotchas: Input 1 is the signal being recorded, input 2 is the listen gate, and input 3 resets.
While listen is on, the input passes through; once listen turns off, the captured segment loops.
Fit to Nearest Cycle uses beat-derived timing; with it off, the loop period is the actual recording duration.
Blend Time is needed for seamless loops but can smear sharp gestures.
Derivative recommends the gestureCapture palette component when a richer capture UI is needed.
